analysis: Changed behavior is limited to CI configuration. In .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 149-155 the Release Integrity job gains a step running three Python scripts on checked-out repo content (test-check-date-comparisons.py, test-check-provider-weak-imports.py, check-date-comparisons.py). The step uses no secrets and no new third-party actions, and the job keeps the workflow's `contents: read` permission. The `.github/workflows/provider-release-cache.yml` patch only adds `scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py` to a path trigger list (line 25). I traced these changes against the threat model assets and boundaries: the provider wire protocol, key custody, attestation, prefix-cache storage (T-041) and sandbox/add-on boundaries (TB-012, TB-013) are untouched, and no runtime provider code changed. The new CI check is a defensive, build-quality gate on provider source and binaries (weak imports and back-deployed Date comparisons), so it does not weaken any control. The existing pull_request trigger runs repo scripts with a read-only token, and `SAVE_CACHES` still limits cache saves to pushes to master and dev, so no new cache-poisoning surface was introduced. The patch for provider-release-cache.yml (bc478b95517c748e:0) is metadata-only with an empty diff beyond the one path line. Remaining question for integration: the contents of the referenced scripts are not supplied, so I cannot verify that they behave as described. That affects CI quality only, not a runtime security conclusion, and I identified no concrete regression.
